title: Modules over a ring form an abelian category with enough injectives
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $\Mod(R)$ the category of $R$-modules and $R$-linear maps. Then $\Mod(R)$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with kernels, cokernels and images the usual ones (so a morphism is a monomorphism iff it is injective), and it has enough injectives: for every $R$-module $M$ there are an injective object $J$ of $\Mod(R)$ (an *injective $R$-module*) [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and an injective $R$-linear map $j:M\to J$.
